1.note: Literally "the rims (backs) of her eyes", read here as the eyebrows, the two dark "rows" of the next words.

2.note: A pun: עַלְמָה (maiden) and נֶעְלֶמֶת (hidden away) come from the same letters.

3.note: A rhyme play: לְחָיַי (my cheeks) closes this line and חַיַּי (my life) the lines before and after it.

4.note: צַוְּרֹנַיִךְ in Song 4:9 is a necklace; here the word stands for the neck itself.

5.he: מִכָּל אֲשֶׁר זָכַר. כִּי הוּא זָכָר
5.note: A pun: זָכַר (he mentioned) and זָכָר (a male) have the same letters. The "maiden" is a man in disguise, and from here on the Hebrew calls the rider "he".

6.note: חָלַץ נַעַל is the ritual of ḥalitzah, the drawing off of the shoe of a man who will not marry his brother's widow (Deut 25:9). The rider mocks Ḥever with it, and calls it an "honor".
